claimBoundary: The analysis makes no freedom-from-interference claim. It reads the phase 8 realization at the named model revision and no run: it shows the part of the driving command that the model names for each of a loss, a delay, a repetition and a corruption on the Eclipse S-CORE path, and the rule by which the actuation adapter detects each; it shows no built program detecting anything. The detection it shows is bounded: a loss is detected only when a later command arrives; a delay only beyond 0.1 s of simulation time against the adapter's newest world time; a corruption only as far as the CRC-32 detects it, for which the model states no residual rate. The detection and the rejection sit in the actuation adapter, a context realization outside the candidate; the candidate's share is the form of the command.

findings.verdict_effect: none (the criterion asks for the part, which is named)
findings.text: A loss is detected by the sequence count of the next command that arrives. A loss after which no command arrives (a trailing loss, a stopped path) is detected by no part of any command: the adapter has no stop response and no watchdog, and the realization names no time-out on the absence of commands.

evidence.quote: a loss or a corruption costs the lost or corrupted command and the next one, which reveals the gap; none of them makes later valid commands fail.
It applies nothing in place of a rejected command: the simulator keeps the last valid control. It has no stop response of its own.

findings.text: The reference count is the highest count among commands whose check value holds. A corruption that the CRC-32 misses and that raises the count would become the reference, and later valid commands would be rejected as repetitions. The realization says 'none of them makes later valid commands fail' (PSR:629-631, 1286-1287) without limiting it to detected corruptions; the bench code states the limit (actuation_core.h:44-47), the model does not. Return to the realization's owner as a wording finding.

A corruption that the check value misses is not one of them: with a higher count it would become the reference, and later valid commands would be repetitions.
